beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Rohan opens his card app. Balance, $5,000. Minimum due, just $150. He pays it, on time, and feels fine.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Keep doing exactly that, and this balance ends up costing him $11,638. 2.3× what he owes today.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Wait, what? But I never miss a payment!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Millions of people do exactly what Rohan does. It feels responsible. The bill is paid, nothing is late, and the card keeps working.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So in the next few minutes: how long the minimum really takes, how much it really costs, and the one line on your statement that fixes it.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Paying the minimum is like running on a treadmill, Rohan. You work hard every month, and the belt keeps pulling you back.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Each payment is a step forward. Each month of interest is the belt, dragging him back almost as fast.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His card charges 1.85% a month on whatever he still owes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That sounds tiny. But over a year it adds up to 22.2%. And because interest is charged on interest, it really works out to about 25%.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Okay, but I pay $150 every single month. That has to add up.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here is how that minimum is worked out. It is a small slice of the balance, 3% on this card. Total owed, $5,000. Minimum, $150.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So he pays. Then interest is charged on everything that is left, and a big part of his payment is simply eaten by next month's interest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now the sneaky part. As the balance shrinks, the minimum shrinks with it. His steps get smaller, right when he should be speeding up.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: The minimum is not built to get you out. It is built to keep you in.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Twelve months go by. Rohan pays the minimum every single time. Never late, not once.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By now, he has paid $1,685. And he still owes $4,323.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: I paid all that, and I still owe that much?

lines.text: Only the rest cut the debt

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Because $1,008 of what he paid went straight to interest. Only the rest touched the actual debt.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It is like filling a bucket with a hole in the bottom. A big share of what he pours in leaks straight back out.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: And Rohan? That was the good year.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here is his balance if he keeps paying only the minimum, month after month. Red is what he still owes. Green is everything he has paid.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Look how the line flattens out. The smaller the balance, the smaller the minimum, so the last stretch drags on for years.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In total, it takes 199 monthly payments. That is about 17 years.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Years? I'll be paying this off longer than I have been working!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By the time this card is cleared, Rohan could change jobs, move cities, maybe start a family. And still be paying for this year's shopping.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: All in, he pays $11,638 to clear $5,000. And $6,638 of that is pure interest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Every dinner, every flight, every gadget on that card ends up costing about 2.3× its price tag.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: In my bank days, we had a name for people who paid only the minimum. Our best customers. They never complained, and they never left.

lines.text: Our maths is the kind version
No grace period on new buys

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And our maths is the kind version. Carry a balance, and most cards stop giving you the interest free grace period on new purchases. Late fees come on top.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So the real bill is even bigger?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Usually, yes. So you stop playing their game. You change one rule.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Same card. Same $5,000. Same rate. One change. Instead of the minimum, Rohan picks one fixed payment, and never lets it shrink.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: To clear the whole balance in three years, that payment is $191 a month.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His very first minimum was $150. The fixed payment is $191. Not a giant leap at the start.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: That's it? I can find that.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: The trick is that it never shrinks. Same big step on the treadmill, every month, while the belt keeps slowing down.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: As the balance falls, interest has less to chew on. So more of every payment hits the debt, and the debt falls faster and faster.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: 36 payments. And then it is gone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now side by side. Paying the minimum, the interest is $6,638, over about 17 years. The fixed payment, $1,893, over three.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Same debt, same rate. The minimum route costs $11,638 in total. The fixed route, $6,893.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Years sooner, and thousands less? Why did nobody tell me?

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Somebody did. It is printed on your statement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In the US, card statements carry a minimum payment warning. It shows how long you will be paying if you pay only the minimum, and what that will cost in total.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: For a balance like this one, there is a second line. The monthly payment that clears the balance in three years, and what that would cost.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: That number is the fix. No calculator needed. The card company has already done the maths for you.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Found it. It has been sitting there every month.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: So here is what Rohan does this week. Three steps.

items.text: No new spending on this card

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: One. Find the three year payment on the statement, and set autopay for that amount. Not the minimum.

items.text: No new spending on this card

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Two. Stop adding new spending to this card while he clears it. Otherwise the belt speeds up again.

items.text: No new spending on this card

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Three. In a good month, pay a little extra. Every extra dollar goes straight at the balance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: One honest catch. If even that payment does not fit the budget, keep paying at least the minimum. A missed payment brings late fees and can push the rate even higher.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: And then pick up the phone. Ask the card company for a lower rate or a payment plan. Asking costs nothing.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Autopay set. Fixed payment. Not the minimum.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So. Minimum only: about 17 years and $11,638. One fixed payment: 36 months and $6,893. Same card, same balance.

params.cta: Find the three year line on your statement
params.assumption: Assumes 22.2% a year charged monthly, a minimum of 3% of the balance and no new spending. Real card formulas and fees differ.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Our maths is simplified, so real cards usually cost a bit more. Follow the panchayat for one money question, settled with real maths.
